title: Tandem immuno-purification of affinity-tagged proteins from mouse testis extracts for MS analysis
protocol: Collect testes for preparation of testis extracts.
Homogenize collected testes in PBS.
Extract cytosolic proteins from homogenized testis tissue.
Remove testes from juvenile male mock control mice and 3xFLAG-HA-tagged knock-in mice (postnatal day 10–21).
Detunicate the testes with fine tweezers in PBS.
Collect detunicated testes into a new 15 mL tube.
Pass clumps of seminiferous tubules through a syringe, noting the presence of interstitial cells.
Homogenize the testes using a Potter-type tissue grinder.
Remove insoluble debris by passing the homogenate through a cell strainer.
Transfer testis extracts into ultra-centrifuge tubes and perform ultra-centrifugation.
Take the clear supernatant from the tube, which is the chromatin-unbound fraction, into a new tube at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in buffer B.
Briefly sonicate the resuspended pellet.
Prepare gel pieces for mass spectrometry analysis.
Snap freeze the collected testes in liquid nitrogen, and store at −80°C until the preparation of extracts.
Resuspend the testes in 10 mL of buffer A at 4°C.
Pass the seminiferous tubules through 1 mm syringe to remove interstitial cells of the testis.
Collect clumps of seminiferous tubules with forceps and place them in a new 10 mL of buffer A at 4°C.
Homogenize the testes with Potter-type tissue grinder pestle and tube by 5–10 strokes at 4°C.
Take 10 μL of homogenate on a slide glass to confirm cells are disrupted.
Hold a cell strainer (100 μm) on top of a 50 mL tube.
Pipette homogenized testis extract and filter it through the cell strainer to remove debris.
Change the cell strainer with a new one if stuck.
Transfer homogenized testis extracts to Open-Top Thickwall Polycarbonate ultra-centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge testis extracts by ultra-centrifugation at 100,000 g for 30 min at 4°C with TLA100.3 Fixed-Angle Titanium Rotor.
Take the supernatant into a new tube at 4°C.
Keep 40 μL of cytosolic extract as input sample for immunoprecipitation if needed later by western blot.
Optional: Store insoluble pellet at −80°C until preparation of nuclear extracts.
Resuspend the insoluble pellet with 5 mL of buffer B at 4°C.
Transfer the suspension into a new tube.
Sonicate the pellet briefly using sonifier 250 with 1/8″ Tapered Microtip or equivalent sonicator.
Incubate the sample at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer homogenized testis extracts to Open-Top Thickwall Polycarbonate ultra-centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the solubilized extracts by ultra-centrifugation at 100,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Take supernatant (total 5 mL) into a new tube at 4°C.
Keep a small amount (20 μL: 0.4% of the starting volume) of nuclear extract at -80°C as input sample for immunoprecipitation, if needed later by western blot.

Equilibrate 100 μL of anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads with buffer A by taking 100 μL of anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads into a tube, place it on a magnetic stand, remove the supernatant, and suspend the anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads in 1 mL of buffer A.
Repeat the wash twice using buffer A.
After the final wash, suspend the magnetic beads in 100 μL of buffer A.
Add 100 μL of anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads suspension to the 10 mL extract.
Incubate for 1–3 hours at 4°C with rotation.
Collect 1.5 mL of the mixture of the extract and anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Place on a magnetic stand and remove the unbound supernatant.
Repeat for the whole mixture of the extract and anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads by collecting 1.5 mL each time into the same tube.
Wash anti-FLAG M2 magnetic beads with 1 mL of buffer A for 4 times on a magnetic stand.
Leave the tubes on the magnetic stand for 1 minute at each wash.
After the final wash, keep the tubes on the magnetic stand.
Remove the washing buffer and suspend the magnetic beads in 200 μL of buffer A containing 3xFLAG peptide (final 100 μg/mL) at 4°C.
Elute bead-bound immunoprecipitates with 200 μL of buffer A containing 3xFLAG peptide at 4°C with rotation for 5 minutes.
Place the tube on a magnetic stand.
Transfer the supernatant into a new tube.
Store 20 μL of the eluted samples at −80°C for later verification.
Repeat elution with another 200 μL of buffer A containing 3xFLAG peptide and combine the eluates.
Equilibrate 100 μL of anti-HA magnetic beads with buffer A.
Place the tube on a magnetic stand, remove the supernatant and suspend the beads in 1 mL of buffer A.
Repeat the wash twice using buffer A.
Suspend the magnetic beads in 100 μL of buffer A after the final wash.
Add 50 μL of anti-HA magnetic beads suspension to FLAG-purified immunoprecipitates from mock control and 3xFLAG-HA-tagged knock-in mice.
Incubate for 1–3 h at 4°C with rotation.
Wash anti-HA magnetic beads with buffer A four times on a magnetic stand.
Remove the supernatant and suspend the magnetic beads in 40 μL of acid elution buffer.
Elute bead-bound immunoprecipitates with gentle tapping for 2 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Place the tube on a magnetic stand after elution.
Remove the supernatant and transfer it into a new tube.
Neutralize the supernatant with 4 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 8.0).
Reconstitute beads-bound immunoprecipitates with acid elution buffer.
Avoid boiling the beads-bound immunoprecipitates in SDS-sample buffer.
Elute IgG from the beads using HA peptide as an alternative to acid elution if needed.
Store immunoprecipitated samples at -80°C until MS analysis.
Run SDS-PAGE using 4 μL of final immunoprecipitates.
Perform western blotting with anti-FLAG or anti-HA antibody.
Run immunoprecipitates on a gel by 0.5–1 cm from the well.
Excise gel pieces containing the protein of interest.
Reduce S-S bonds and alkylate the excised gel pieces.
Digest peptides in gel using trypsin.
Elute peptides from the gel.
Subject eluted peptides to LC-MS/MS analysis for identification.
Alternatively, perform acid elution on whole immunoprecipitates directly for MS shotgun analysis.
Use buffer B without detergents at the final washing step for in-liquid digestion.
Boil immunoprecipitated samples in NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer with Sample Reducing Agent at 90°C for 5 min.
Run the samples on a NuPAGE 4%–12% Bis-Tris gel in MOPS-SDS buffer with antioxidant at 200 V for 3–5 min.
Immerse the gel in pure water for 10 min with rotation.
Stain the gel in Simply Blue solution for > 2 h.
Discard the Simply Blue solution and wash the gel in pure water.
Excise a gel slice approximately 0.8 cm × 0.5 cm immediately below the wells.
Cut the excised gel slices into approximately 1–1.5 mm sized cubes.
Transfer the gel cubes into a 1.5 mL Protein LoBind micro-tube.
Destain the protein bands in gel pieces with 300 μL of 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate, 50% acetonitrile for 10–15 min by shaking at room temperature at 900 rpm.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Destain the protein bands in gel pieces with 300 μL of 40 mM ammonium bicarbonate, 20% acetonitrile for 10–15 min.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Repeat the destaining steps once more.
Dehydrate the gel pieces with 150 μL of acetonitrile for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Finally, dehydrate the gel pieces with a centrifugal evaporator for 15 min.
After dehydration, reduce the proteins in the gel pieces with 200 μL of 10 mM DTT in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate for 1 h at 56°C.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Wash the gel pieces with 100–150 μL of 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Alkylate proteins in the gel pieces with 100–150 μL of 55 mM iodoacetamide in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate for 45 min with protection from light.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Wash the gel pieces with 100–150 μL of 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant and discard.
Dehydrate gel pieces with 300 μL of 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate and 50% acetonitrile for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and discard it.
Repeat step 39 once more.
Dehydrate gel pieces with a centrifugal evaporator for 15 minutes.
Digest proteins in gel pieces with 20 ng/μL trypsin and lysyl endopeptidase in 40 mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer, pH 8.0, overnight at 37°C by shaking at 650 rpm.
Wait until the gel pieces expand with the solution of trypsin and lysyl endopeptidase on ice for about 1 hour before covering them with 40 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Extract digested peptides from gel pieces with 50–100 μL of 50% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid for 30–60 minutes at room temperature in the Maximizer at 1,300 rpm.
Remove supernatant and transfer it into a fresh micro-tube.
Re-extract digested peptides from gel pieces with 50–100 μL of 70% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid for 30–60 minutes at room temperature in the Maximizer at 1,300 rpm.
Remove supernatant and transfer it into the micro-tube from step 42.
Concentrate combined supernatant to 15 μL with a centrifugal evaporator.
Perform mass calibration for positive ion mode using LTQ Velos ESI Positive Ion Calibration Solution.
Set MS range to m/z 350–2,000 with a resolution of 70,000 in positive ion mode.
Acquire MS/MS spectra using Top-10 DDA settings with a resolution of 17,500 and high-energy collision dissociation value of 27.
Set ESI spray parameters to 1,400 V, 250°C, and 500 nL/min using the Advance Captive Spray Ionization probe.
Inject sample from autosampler into a pre-column through the multi-valve.
Trap injected sample in the pre-column (L-column 2 ODS, 5 μm, 0.3 × 5 mm).
Desalt and concentrate the trapped sample using solvent consisting of 2% acetonitrile and 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid.
Dilute samples two-fold with a solvent mixture of 2% acetonitrile and 0.1% trifluoroacetic acid for desalting and concentration.
Change the position of the multi-valve to connect it to the separation column line after sample treatment.
Set up the separation column micro-ODS column (L-column 2 ODS, 3 μm, 0.1 × 150 mm) at 40°C with flow rate 500 nL/min.
Prepare mobile phase A using LCMS grade water containing 0.1% formic acid.
Prepare mobile phase B using LCMS grade acetonitrile containing 0.1% formic acid.
Perform continuous injection with the auto-sampler controlled by Xcalibur/Tune (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Set fixed modification to carbamidomethylation of Cys in Proteome Discoverer version 1.4 (Thermo Fisher) using Mascot search engine version 2.7 (Matrix Science).
Optionally set variable modifications: oxidation of Met, deamidation of Asn, and deamidation of Gln.
Set precursor mass tolerance to 10 ppm in the analysis parameters.
Set fragment ion mass tolerance to 0.02 Da for accurate data interpretation.
Estimate the false discovery rate (FDR) using a decoy database composed of either randomized or reversed sequences from the target database.
Evaluate false positives using the Percolator algorithm.
Filter the search results to maintain a 1% global FDR for high confidence level.
